correctness.rationale: For every integer dimension at least two and all positive coordinate conductances, the square-root-weighted incidence construction defines the Euclidean-orthogonal cut projector. The exact tensor-product heat kernel gives the sign of every entry and yields the claimed unit parallel-direction absolute current and pairwise transverse contributions. A separate Laplace expansion proves the finite-subset formula for each diagonal and hence the complementary cycle-column formula. Strict scalar-kernel monotonicity proves the geometric-profile cut maximizers. An exact diagonal-order comparison reduces the four-dimensional cycle maximizer to only two possible directions. The rational factorization of their difference is independently reconstructed from the formulas, and exact Sturm variations decreasing from 13 to 11 establish exactly two simple roots above one, in the two stated rational intervals, with signs positive, negative, positive. The standalone checker reconstructed all 188 columns from exact grounded Laplacians in eight graphs and verified the polynomial identity, coprimality with its derivative and Sturm counts. Finite graph tests corroborate the general analytic proof rather than replacing it.

originality.rationale: The 2023 Hamming-cube theorem determines the equal-conductance endpoint norm, and the 2026 weighted transfer-current theorem bounds the global spectral norm of the entrywise absolute symmetric transfer-current matrix; neither implies arbitrary direction-dependent exact endpoint columns nor two reentrant maximizing-direction changes. Searches for anisotropic cut projections, weighted Hamming currents, exact transfer-current endpoint norms, and reentrant geometric weight directions yielded no decisive covering statement. Existing public mathematical-record hits on Walsh spectral projections concern a different space/operator. Because indexed-search gaps and possible implicit older network calculations remain, the assessment is best-knowledge and not a claim of proven uniqueness.

value.rationale: The symmetric weighted transfer-current projector is a standard object in graph electrical flow and Banach-space endpoint operator geometry. The theorem replaces exponentially many edge-column evaluations by pairwise-weight sums and a finite subset formula valid for arbitrary positive directional conductances. Geometrically increasing weights yield a sharp middle-direction cut maximizer in every dimension and, in dimension four, exactly two reentrant switches for the complementary cycle maximizer. The thresholds are rigorously root-counted rather than extrapolated from a finite numerical sample. This produces a natural, nonmonotone sensitivity example for complementary Hodge projections, not a recomputed known table.
